items.title: Kremlin says Putin and Trump discussed Ukraine settlement without major announcements
items.summary: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin and Trump discussed the war in Ukraine and bilateral relations during their meeting. He described the talks positively but said neither side made major announcements, with further statements expected after a trilateral meeting involving China.

items.title: Russian strikes reportedly target Odesa port infrastructure and Sumy substation
items.summary: Russian military-linked reports say overnight strikes hit two electricity substations supporting Odesa-area ports, fuel-storage facilities at Chornomorsk and a 330-kilovolt substation in Sumy. They also claim a cargo ship carrying dual-use supplies toward Odesa was struck at sea; the extent of damage was not specified.

items.title: Russian battlefield report claims advances in Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Kharkiv
items.summary: A Russian frontline assessment reports advances northeast of Ternuvate in Zaporizhzhia, entry into Mykolaipillia on the Kostiantynivka axis and fighting inside Borova in Kharkiv region. The report also describes continued clashes near Lyman and Kupiansk without establishing independently assessed changes to control.

items.title: Danish MEP proposes sweeping Russian concessions as preconditions for peace talks
items.summary: Danish European Parliament member Henrik Dahl reportedly proposed that Russia withdraw from Ukraine and several other regions, relinquish Kaliningrad and its UN Security Council seat, and sharply limit its armed forces before peace negotiations begin. These are a lawmaker's proposed demands, not an agreed European negotiating position.

items.title: SAPO reports bail set for lawyer suspected in $45,000 corruption scheme
items.summary: SAPO says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court set bail at 998,000 hryvnias for a lawyer suspected of encouraging a bribery scheme involving a serving prosecutor. Investigators allege she received $45,000 while claiming she could arrange the closure of a criminal case, but kept the money rather than passing it to the prosecutor. The case remains at the suspicion stage.

items.title: Dutch company reportedly details RUTA missile role in Crimean Bridge attacks
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report says Dutch firm Destinus acknowledged that its RUTA drone-missiles were used against the Crimean Bridge on consecutive days, including seven reported hits that caused a span to collapse. The report also attributes electronic-warfare support to the company's systems and says Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen declined to address parliamentary questions about the firm's involvement.

items.title: Kursk governor reports Ukrainian drone attack in city centre
items.summary: Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein reported a Ukrainian drone attack on the city, with preliminary accounts indicating smoke inside a building in the centre. The initial report did not specify casualties or the extent of damage.

items.title: Trump says he and Xi want to help end Russia–Ukraine war
items.summary: President Donald Trump said he and Chinese President Xi Jinping want to help bring the Russia–Ukraine conflict to an end. Trump described his meeting with Vladimir Putin as preparation for trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States and China, without announcing a settlement.

items.title: Russian Foreign Ministry challenges UNESCO report on journalists killed in war
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused UNESCO's latest journalist-safety report of omitting Russian correspondents killed during the conflict. Moscow says it will press UNESCO to revise its casualty-recording methodology and include the named journalists in its statistics; the allegations are Russia's stated position.

items.title: Kushner travels to Berlin for talks on Ukraine settlement
items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner is reportedly heading to Berlin for discussions with President Volodymyr Zelensky and European political leaders about a possible settlement of the Russia–Ukraine war. The meetings follow previously announced plans for negotiations involving US, Ukrainian and European representatives.

items.title: Russia says military prosthetics waiting lists eliminated
items.summary: Russian Deputy Defence Minister Anna Tsivileva said waiting lists for prosthetic treatment in military hospitals have been eliminated and the average process from injury to discharge has fallen to about three months. She also reported eight hospitals built or modernized in 2026, adding 1,500 beds, and described simplified compensation procedures for wounded service members.

items.title: Spanish police investigate far-right group with alleged Ukraine training links
items.summary: A report about Spain's Núcleo Nacional group says investigators are examining alleged paramilitary training by members in Ukraine and contacts with the Azov brigade, amid an inquiry into a possible armed uprising. A separate analysis reportedly argued the group's activity benefited Russian interests but did not establish Russian financing or operational control.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry claims drone strikes on Ukrainian equipment
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says drones operated by its Tsentr Group destroyed Ukrainian heavy hexacopters and communications equipment in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. The statement did not provide quantities or a detailed damage assessment.
